introduction: I study Artificial Intelligence at Xi'an Jiaotong University and work as a research assistant in Prof. Tengfei Luo's group at the University of Notre Dame. GPU-memory limitations in my UMA / FAIR-Chem polymer-simulation work sparked my interest in making ML interatomic potentials more efficient.
biography: I am a fourth-year undergraduate majoring in Artificial Intelligence in the Artificial Intelligence Experimental Class at Xi'an Jiaotong University. I am also a research assistant in Prof. Tengfei Luo's group in the Department of Aerospace and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Notre Dame.

I enrolled at Xi'an Jiaotong University in 2023 and expect to graduate in 2027. I have been a research assistant at Notre Dame since October 2025. I was a visiting student at Notre Dame from August to December 2025 and returned for summer research through iSURE from July to September 2026.

Working on polymer simulations with UMA / FAIR-Chem exposed me to GPU-memory constraints in practice. That experience led me to ask how ML interatomic potentials could use computational resources more efficiently. I am interested in understanding computational redundancy, reducing memory requirements, and improving simulation throughput while preserving useful physical predictions.
My research interests also include JEPA-style representation learning for molecular dynamics, coarse-grained modeling, and polymer property prediction.
